edges.act_citation_note:
THE INSTRUMENT IS NAMED, DATED AND PAGED BY THE BOOK'S OWN TABLE OF CONTENTS AND
ITS TEXT WAS NOT READ. The contents leaf lists `Motu Proprio Benedicti PP. XV
« Cum iuris canonici », 15 Septembris 1917 ... xliii`, between the constitution
at p. xxxix and the profession of faith at p. xlv, so the document exists, is
dated to the day, and stands three leaves further on in the very copy this
record reads.

It is drawn as a station rather than dropped because a record that lists what
its own witness's contents page lists, minus the entries it could not read, is a
record whose absences are invisible.
edges.act_citation_scope:
The corpus searched is ONE FILE: the Internet Archive optical-character-
recognition text layer of the 1918 Vatican Polyglot printing, item
codexiuriscanoni00cath, sha256 16f72ea3..., 2,863,036 bytes, which this
repository registers as an artifact. A normalised whole-file search of it for
`cum iuris canonici` returns exactly one hit and that hit is the table of
contents line at the head of the file; there is no second occurrence anywhere.

THAT IS A STATEMENT ABOUT ONE SCAN AND ABOUT NOTHING ELSE. The Roman-numbered
front leaves of that copy are the part of it the scanner served worst, and the
constitution three leaves earlier survives in it only as a paraphrase in the
praefatio. It was NOT searched for in the Acta Apostolicae Sedis of 1917, which
would settle it, nor in any other printing of the Code, nor on vatican.va. Not
found here means not in that file.
edges.parent_basis:
Two acts of one Pope about one Code, four months apart, printed one after the
other in the front matter of the same book. Neither was read naming the other,
because the second was not read at all.
